label: Nova-C-class lander, 14-day mission
description: The default: a lander like Intuitive Machines' Nova-C (700 Wh battery, 200 W of panels), working for 14 days, with Earth counted as soon as any part of it shows above the horizon.
payloads: Landing sensors (NDL lidar, SCALPSS plume cameras), radio and navigation beacons (LN-1) and power-hungry science (PRIME-1 drill and mass spectrometer), as flown on IM-1 and IM-2.

label: Long mission: 28 days
description: The same lander, asked to work for 28 days: about one full lunar day and night, so the site has to get it through a long darkness and keep Earth in view for half of a longer mission.
payloads: Long-duration science that must outlast a lunar night: heat-flow probes and seismometers (CLPS Blue Ghost carried the LISTER heat-flow drill).

label: Weak antenna: Earth 2° above the horizon
description: The same lander and 14 days, but its antenna only links when Earth clears the horizon by 2° (a terrain or antenna mask), instead of as soon as any part of Earth shows.
payloads: Communication-heavy payloads with a low or partly blocked antenna, such as a radio beacon or a surface network (IM-2 carried a Nokia 4G/LTE network).
